text:
elaine: Triage from today's RFC: we need a decision on trace header compression. Options: full header passthrough (no compression), wire compression with a fixed dictionary, or adaptive delta/dictionary per-producer. Main tension = network/cost savings vs losing attribute cardinality for cost attribution and ad-hoc queries.

rob: Full passthrough is simplest for correctness: every attribute available downstream, no decoding needed. Downsides: high egress on mobile/edge producers and more bytes in our ingest pipeline. Not ideal for sites with limited uplink.

ivor: Fixed dictionary compression looks attractive: we maintain a canonical dictionary of common attribute keys and high-frequency values (env, region, sdk_version). Producers send small integer codes for keys. Pros: deterministic, fast to decode, small footprint. Cons: dictionary drift and new keys cause fallback full-key encoding.

tia: Adaptive per-producer dictionaries reduce misses but make downstream aggregation harder: different shards may see different code maps for the same logical key leading to cardinality explosions unless we normalize at ingress. That defeats the network savings if we normalize early.

elaine: We measured a sample of 48h of mobile traces: header payload accounts for ~22% of bytes and 65% of that is a long list of low-cardinality attributes (env, svc, region) plus a long tail of rare keys. Query: top keys by frequency, small tail but many unique keys.

elaine: ```sql
SELECT key, count(*) as freq
FROM trace_headers_48h
GROUP BY key
ORDER BY freq DESC
LIMIT 50;
-- top keys ~ 85% of traffic, long tail of thousands
```

ingest-bot: FYI: new client SDKs support header compression flags: X-Trace-Header-Comp: dict-v1 or delta.

rob: Proposal A (ingress-normalizing fixed-dictionary): accept dict-v1 from producers but ingress expands codes to canonical keys before writing to storage. Storage contains full keys (no loss). This gives wire savings without downstream cardinality issues. Cost: CPU/alloc at ingress to expand keys and occasional dictionary fetch.

ivor: Proposal B (pass-through compressed, de-duped at query): store compressed payloads as-is and add a translation index mapping (producer_id, dict_version) -> canonical keys. Queries that need keys must consult the index and decode on-read. Pro: cheaper ingest CPU. Con: query-time decode increases latency and complexity for joins and cost attribution.

tia: Proposal C (hybrid): keep a small canonical dictionary at ingress; producers can send codes. If a code is unknown, ingress requests the producer's dictionary async and temporarily stores the raw key. Maintain a background normalizer that reconciles new keys into canonical namespace and backfills storage with normalized tokens. Provides fast path and graceful upgrade. Complexity is higher.

elaine: Important constraints: 1) cost attribution relies on stable keys (e.g., billing_key, tenant_id) — any compression scheme must guarantee those keys are available and canonical when we do aggregation; 2) low-latency checks (alerts/SLOs) can't pay a heavy decode cost; 3) we must be robust to malicious/malformed dictionaries.

rob: For billing keys specifically, we should require plain-text passthrough (no code) unless the producer proves mapping to canonical key via signed dictionary snapshot. That keeps billing stable. In other words, sensitive or high-cardinality keys are exempt from compression.

ivor: Operational model: if ingress needs to expand dict codes we should cache dictionaries in memory with a small LRU and metricize cache hit rate `dict_expand_hit_ratio`. Misses -> fetch from metadata store (S3/KV) and instrument latency. Excessive misses cause a producer-level alert.

tia: We should add a schema/tariff: stable keys (billing_key, tenant, customer_region, sdk_version) must be either plain-text or part of the canonical global dictionary. Other keys may be compressed. Producers should declare which mode with `X-Trace-Header-Comp: mode=opt-in;dict=global` header.

elaine: Security note: dictionaries are authority-signed to avoid spoofing. Ingress will validate a dictionary signature and version. Unsigned dictionaries are rejected — producers must fall back to plain headers.

rob: Performance sketch: expanding a compressed header costs ~200ns per key decode in C++ path; network bytes saved per trace ~120B average. At 100k/s traces that's ~12MB/s savings, so ingress CPU cost is small compared to network savings. Need to validate on canary.

ivor: Query-side impact for Proposal B: decode-on-read means every analytic job must join with dict index; this blows up cost for frequent queries. Not acceptable for billing pipelines.

tia: Suggestion: implement Proposal A with an opt-in global dictionary and strict rule that billing-critical keys are never encoded. Keep Proposal B as a low-cost ingest-only experiment for internal debug traces where query-load is low.

elaine: Action items: 1) rob: draft global-dictionary format + signing scheme and an ingress expander interface; 2) ivor: add dict fetch/cache to ingress with metrics; 3) tia: update SDK docs and create a producer checklist for keys that must stay plaintext; 4) ops: define canary with traffic mirror of 5% mobile writes for 3 days and measure CPU, p50 write latency, and billing pipeline correctness.

ingest-bot: Ticket PROJ-1182 created: "Global trace-header dictionary + ingress normalization POC" assigned to rob, ivor, tia

rob: I'll prototype the expand-only path and a feature-flagged flow that rejects unsigned dicts. 

ivor: I'll model cache size and TTL. Early estimate: 10k dictionaries in cache, TTL 1h, mem ~80MB.

tia: Canary acceptance: billing aggregation unchanged, p50 ingest write latency delta <6ms, dict_expand_hit_ratio >= 98% on canary. If any billing discrepancy -> block rollout.

elaine: Thanks everyone. If you have objections to the global-dictionary + ingress-normalize recommendation speak up now, otherwise I'll create the follow-ups and schedule a short design review.

rob: +1 from me.

ivor: +1. Will open the PR for the ingress cache bits.

tia: +1. Will update SDK docs PR.

elaine: Closing thread. Follow-up sync Friday to approve the POC design.
